title: Judges 4
paragraphs: ¹ After Ehud died, the Israelites again did evil in the LORD's sight. ² So the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who ruled in Hazor. His army commander was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-haggoyim. ³ Because Jabin had nine hundred iron chariots and had cruelly oppressed the Israelites for twenty years, they cried out to the LORD for help. ⁴ Now Deborah, a prophet, the wife of Lappidoth, was leading Israel at that time. ⁵ She held court under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came to her to have their disputes settled.

⁶ She sent for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and said to him, "Has the LORD God of Israel not commanded you: 'Go, march to Mount Tabor and take ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun with you'? ⁷ I will draw Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, with his chariots and troops, to the Kishon River, and hand him over to you." ⁸ Barak answered her, "If you go with me, I'll go; but if you don't go with me, I won't go." ⁹ "I will certainly go with you," she said, "but the road you're taking will bring you no glory, because the LORD will hand Sisera over to a woman." So Deborah got up and went with Barak to Kedesh. ¹⁰ Barak summoned Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh, and ten thousand men followed him. Deborah went up with him as well.

¹¹ Now Heber the Kenite — a descendant of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law — had separated from the other Kenites and pitched his tent near the great tree at Zaanannim, near Kedesh. ¹² When Sisera was told that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor, ¹³ he called together all nine hundred of his iron chariots and all the troops he had, marching from Harosheth-haggoyim to the Kishon River. ¹⁴ Then Deborah said to Barak, "Go! This is the day the LORD has given Sisera into your hands. Has not the LORD gone ahead of you?" So Barak charged down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men behind him. ¹⁵ The LORD threw Sisera, all his chariots, and his entire army into a panic before Barak's sword. Sisera abandoned his chariot and fled on foot.

¹⁶ Barak pursued the chariots and the army all the way to Harosheth-haggoyim. The whole army of Sisera fell by the sword; not one man was left. ¹⁷ But Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, because Jabin king of Hazor and the family of Heber the Kenite were at peace. ¹⁸ Jael came out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Come in, my lord, come right in. Don't be afraid." So he went into her tent, and she covered him with a blanket. ¹⁹ He said to her, "Please give me some water. I'm thirsty." She opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him up again. ²⁰ "Stand at the entrance to the tent," he told her. "If anyone comes and asks you, 'Is there anyone here?' say no."

²¹ But Jael, Heber's wife, picked up a tent peg and a hammer. While Sisera lay sleeping from exhaustion, she drove the peg through his temple and into the ground, and he died. ²² Just then Barak came by in pursuit of Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. "Come," she said, "I'll show you the man you're looking for." He went in with her, and there lay Sisera, dead, with the tent peg through his temple. ²³ So on that day God subdued Jabin king of Canaan before the Israelites. ²⁴ And the power of Israel grew stronger and stronger against Jabin king of Canaan until they finally destroyed him.
